1GOXN-58Y5R-VNCUE-MUB0F.label: CAPTAIN'S LOG A-01 | Stardate 2143.119.1719
1GOXN-58Y5R-VNCUE-MUB0F.text:
[Log A-01 | Stardate 2143.119.1719]
CAPTAIN'S LOG

Day one of the new research phase. The team is settled.
Morale is good — as good as it gets out here, which is
good enough.

Whatever Dr. Cross and his people are working on in the
research wing, the rest of the crew has stopped asking.
That's how it usually goes. You get curious and then
you get bored of being curious and then you get used to
the closed doors.

Fourteen months to the next supply ship.
We have everything we need.

We have everything we need.

    —— Capt. E. Harrow
[END OF LOG]

1Q3CN-XVPCP-WGX6M-VTV0X.label: CAPTAIN'S LOG A-15 | Stardate 2143.136.2132
1Q3CN-XVPCP-WGX6M-VTV0X.text:
[Log A-15 | Stardate 2143.136.2132]
CAPTAIN'S LOG

Dr. Osei submitted a supplemental sensor report today.
She wouldn't say what it was about. Said it was Cross's
department. I asked Cross.

Cross said it was fine.

I've known Harlan Cross for eleven years. I know what
his "fine" means. It means he's deciding how much
to tell you.

I told him to keep me informed.

He said he would.

    —— Capt. E. Harrow
[END OF LOG]

6RR68-2HTES-9EC73-G1K23.label: POD BAY LOG O-066 | Stardate 2143.162.2205
6RR68-2HTES-9EC73-G1K23.author: O-066
6RR68-2HTES-9EC73-G1K23.text:
[Log O-066 | Stardate 2143.162.2205]
POD BAY LOG

Day forty-four, Sector Seven bay.

Five cradles, five pods, all away by 2140. I released the
last one myself. Nobody told me to stay and nobody told me
to go, so I am writing this and then I am going to sit down.

Each pod seats six. I did not count the people. I counted
the empty seats on the way out and stopped at eleven.

The beacons are dark. I asked three people why and got three
different reasons. All three were frightened, so I believe
all three.

If anyone reads this, the cradles are intact. Whoever left
did it clean.

    —— J. Park, Pod Bay Technician
[END OF LOG]

L1O7J-U38KD-IYXZ4-Y5G29.label: RESEARCH LOG R-142 | Stardate 2143.126.0614
L1O7J-U38KD-IYXZ4-Y5G29.author: R-142
L1O7J-U38KD-IYXZ4-Y5G29.text:
[Log R-142 | Stardate 2143.126.0614]
RESEARCH LOG

Day eight. The run schedule is holding.

This is the third program I have worked in this wing.
The doors close the same way every time. Nobody outside
asks, and nobody inside is allowed to say much, so after
a few weeks the quiet starts to feel like a feature.

Cross runs the floor the way he always has. He wants the
notes tidy, the feeds clean, and the fourteen of us to know
where the line is. I have never needed to ask where it is.

Osei thinks the baseline is too steady. I told her steady
is what a baseline is for.

    —— Dr. R. Ibarra
[END OF LOG]

LN5QJ-X2M7G-JKS6E-4X02I.label: RESEARCH LOG R-157 | Stardate 2143.145.2250
LN5QJ-X2M7G-JKS6E-4X02I.author: R-157
LN5QJ-X2M7G-JKS6E-4X02I.text:
[Log R-157 | Stardate 2143.145.2250]
RESEARCH LOG

Day twenty-seven. Cross has asked that the fourteen of us
sleep in the wing until the current runs are closed. He
calls it continuity. Nobody argued, which tells you how
tired everyone is.

The readings have stopped behaving like the earlier
programs. They do not drift. They arrive, and they stay.

I asked Osei what she thought. She said she had already
written it down, and then she asked me not to ask again.

I am going to try to sleep. The lights in the wing have
started to dim on a schedule none of us set.

    —— Dr. N. Haddad
[END OF LOG]

QTI6N-J595F-ATCV7-THZ2F.label: SECURITY LOG S-087 | Stardate 2143.149.0712
QTI6N-J595F-ATCV7-THZ2F.author: S-087
QTI6N-J595F-ATCV7-THZ2F.text:
[Log S-087 | Stardate 2143.149.0712]
SECURITY LOG

Day thirty-one, end of the first watch.

I took four to the corridor outside the research wing at
0340, on a door alarm that ECH/OES classed routine. Two of
us walked back. I have written what I saw on the incident
form, and the form will say what the system says it will say.

I am putting the rest here because the form will not hold
it. The cameras recorded the whole time. The corridor is
empty on every frame.

I have sealed the ring behind us. I have told nobody else
to go in.

    —— Officer D. Whitlock, Security
[END OF LOG]

R7SY6-BA3LI-OBD0J-AXP03.label: ENGINEERING LOG E-143 | Stardate 2143.150.2352
R7SY6-BA3LI-OBD0J-AXP03.author: E-143
R7SY6-BA3LI-OBD0J-AXP03.text:
[Log E-143 | Stardate 2143.150.2352]
ENGINEERING LOG

Day thirty-two, night watch, rear power supply.

Chief Engineer Cross came to the aft hub with six people
and a written order. The authorization is real. I checked
it twice.

We are emptying the primary cell housings by hand, a bank
at a time, onto carts. The cells are heavy and they do not
like to be carried. Cross told me where they are going and
asked me to put it out of my head. I am doing my best.

When the last bank leaves, everything that runs on the
cells goes dark. The reactor bus keeps the air, the lights
that matter, the pods and the spin. Nothing else.

He has not sat down once.

    —— M. Okonkwo, Engineering
[END OF LOG]

WRY30-WJAXL-Q5U7U-9O61D.label: MEDICAL LOG M-052 | Stardate 2143.152.0618
WRY30-WJAXL-Q5U7U-9O61D.author: M-052
WRY30-WJAXL-Q5U7U-9O61D.text:
[Log M-052 | Stardate 2143.152.0618]
MEDICAL LOG

Day thirty-four. I have finished the triage board and I
cannot make myself look at it again.

Eleven intake forms have no cause of injury on them. When I
asked each patient where it happened they gave me the same
word. Corridor. No deck, no section, as if the ship had
only one. I wrote the word on every form because it was
the only thing they agreed on.

Blood products last two days at this rate. The battery on
the bay unit will outlast the blood.

Three of the ambers have asked whether they should try for
the hubs. I told them I cannot advise that.

    —— Dr. A. Reyes, Medical Bay
[END OF LOG]
